directAnswer: To check a Git merge, you can use the command `git log --merges` to view merge commits or check the status with `git status` after the merge.
summary: This guide provides steps to verify a Git merge and check for any conflicts or issues.

sections.heading: Understanding Git Merge
sections.body: A Git merge combines changes from different branches into a single branch. It's essential to verify that the merge completed successfully and that there are no conflicts.

sections.heading: Checking Merge Commits
sections.body: You can view the history of merge commits using the `git log --merges` command. This will list all the merges that have been performed in the repository.

sections.heading: Verifying Merge Status
sections.body: After performing a merge, use `git status` to check if there are any unmerged paths or conflicts that need to be resolved.

steps.title: View Merge Commits
steps.detail: Run `git log --merges` in your terminal to display a list of all merge commits.

steps.title: Check Current Status
steps.detail: Execute `git status` to see if there are any conflicts or unmerged files after the merge.

steps.title: Review Changes
steps.detail: Use `git diff` to review changes made by the merge, if necessary.

faqs.question: What if I encounter merge conflicts?
faqs.answer: If you have merge conflicts, Git will notify you during the merge process. You will need to manually resolve these conflicts in the affected files.

faqs.question: How can I undo a merge?
faqs.answer: You can undo a merge by using `git merge --abort` if you haven't committed yet, or `git reset --hard HEAD~1` to revert to the previous commit.

faqs.question: Is there a way to visualize merges?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can use tools like Gitk or Git GUI to visualize the commit history and merges in a graphical format.

caveats: The command outputs may vary based on your Git version.
Ensure you have the necessary permissions to view the repository history.
